title: Assessment result
description: A structured diagnostic output. It is a read-only finding and is deliberately a different artifact from a change set, which is what FR-57 means by separating diagnosis from proposed mutation: the two cannot be confused because they do not share a schema. Every finding either cites evidence or declares that it does not. Status and confidence use English identifiers; the original reference values are recorded as provenance in the vocabulary rather than used as identifiers here (FR-03).

scopeContractHash.description: The scope this assessment was produced under. A result read without knowing its scope is a result about an unknown subject.

evidenceManifestHash.description: The canonical hash of the manifest backing this result. Binding to the hash is what stops a result from being paired with a manifest that changed after the fact.

findings.description: Required, and required even when empty. An assessment that found nothing says so explicitly; an absent list would be indistinguishable from an assessment that was never completed.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this schema the instance conforms to (FR-05, FR-29).

identifier.description: Lowercase, hyphen-separated. Constrained so an identifier cannot carry arbitrary text, and English by construction (FR-03, CON-01).

opaqueId.description: An opaque handle, or a placeholder in the angle-bracket form that every shipped example uses.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339, UTC, Z-suffixed. The pattern is present because format is an annotation by default.

sha256Hex.description: Lowercase hex, exactly 64 characters, as ADR-0004 pins.

assessmentStatus.description: Indeterminate is a real outcome rather than a missing one. An assessment that could not reach its sources must be able to say so without borrowing healthy, which would report an absence of evidence as evidence of absence.

confidence.description: How much weight the status carries. Separate from status on purpose: a degraded finding held with low confidence and one held with high confidence call for different responses, and collapsing them loses exactly that distinction.

finding.description: A finding either resolves to evidence or declares its standing, mirroring the conclusion rule in the evidence manifest. Expressed as an exclusive choice so a finding cannot both cite evidence and call itself inferred.

severity.description: Severity of the finding, not of the recommended action. The framework proposes no action, so a severity that implied urgency of remediation would be describing something outside this artifact.

evidenceRefs.description: Entry identifiers in the backing evidence manifest. That each resolves is a semantic check.

classification.description: The explicit standing of a finding that does not resolve to evidence.
